calls.headline: Telecom Egypt's profit rises 44% as MSCI adds it to its Egypt index
calls.body: Telecom Egypt's nine-month net profit rose 44% to EGP 24.4bn on revenue up 19% to EGP 93.6bn, with EBITDA up 24% to EGP 43.1bn, a 46% margin, and net debt down to 0.8 times EBITDA from 1.5 times (company release). Data revenue rose 30% and international incoming calls 25%. Mubasher reported an 88% rise against a lower prior-year figure; the company's own comparison, carried by Youm7 and Hapi Journal, is 44%. Separately, MSCI will add the stock to its Egypt standard index and drop Eastern Company at the close on November 30 (Fintech Gate). Telecom Egypt closed flat at EGP 135.01 on Wednesday after eight straight gains, up 105.3% this year.
calls.view: Index funds tracking MSCI Egypt must buy Telecom Egypt and sell Eastern by November 30, and the results give the buying a fundamental floor: on the last 12 months' profit the stock trades at about 7.7 times earnings. The desk opens a low-confidence view that it holds above EGP 122 into the inclusion; after a doubling, much of this may already be in the price. Eastern faces the mirror image despite a 39% rise in profit.
calls.wrong: Telecom Egypt closes below EGP 122, about 10% lower, before November 30.

calls.headline: Elsewedy, e-finance and Emaar Misr report; growth is uneven
calls.line: Results are strong on the surface, but only some of the growth is repeatable.
calls.body: Elsewedy Electric's nine-month consolidated profit rose 16% to EGP 16.4bn on revenue up 32% to EGP 263bn (Mubasher, Alborsa). e-finance's rose 40% to EGP 2.62bn on revenue up 27% to EGP 6.28bn, and its board proposed about 1.38 free shares per share, subject to the FRA and an extraordinary assembly (Mubasher, Fintech Gate). Emaar Misr's profit rose 129% to EGP 9.83bn (Mubasher), but EGP 7.8bn of that came in the first quarter alone (Hapi Journal). On Wednesday Elsewedy closed at EGP 121.46, e-finance at EGP 24.80 and Emaar Misr at EGP 12.52.
calls.view: e-finance's growth is the cleanest: steady government-payment revenue, with the bonus issue changing only the share count. Elsewedy's margins narrowed as revenue grew twice as fast as profit, a poor fit for a stock up 55% this year and above its 50-day average of about EGP 117.8. Emaar Misr's headline is flattered by one quarter; the desk waits for the filing before reading it as growth.
calls.wrong: Elsewedy closes above EGP 135, a new high well above its range, before the end of November.

calls.headline: EGX30 flat at 52,500; Arabs sell EGP 141.5m, fertilizers lead
calls.line: The index paused at its 50-day average after Tuesday's 2.08% jump, with locals buying.
calls.body: The EGX30 edged up 0.03% to 52,500.47 on Wednesday on turnover of EGP 11.8bn, against Tuesday's EGP 12.8bn. Egyptians bought a net EGP 110.8m and foreigners EGP 30.6m, while Arabs sold EGP 141.5m (Masrawy, Amwal Al Ghad). Abu Qir rose 5.0% to EGP 78.00, Eastern 4.2% and Mopco 2.8%, while Banque du Caire fell 2.7% to EGP 5.70 after its third-quarter profit fell 20% on provisions (EnterpriseAM). The EGX70 EWI slipped 0.26% after six straight gains.
calls.view: A flat day on solid turnover is consolidation, not a top: foreigners were net buyers for a second session, and the index sits just under its 50-day average of about 52,777. Abu Qir's jump is a reaction to nine-month profit that doubled, not to any easing of the 33% gas cut, so the desk keeps its fertilizer view, now with the price against it.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 50,000 before the end of November.

calls.headline: The dollar index hits a 19-month high; the pound eases 0.4%
calls.line: A firmer dollar and talk of a half-point Fed hike test the carry trade before today's bills.
calls.body: The central bank's dollar rate rose to EGP 53.62 on Wednesday from 53.39, a 0.4% fall for the pound, as the dollar index climbed 0.6% to 102.84, its highest since April 2025. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said that if October's prices matched the past two months, "a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting" (Federal Reserve); October core prices rose 0.3%. The Fed meets December 9, eight days before the central bank. The 182- and 364-day bills are auctioned today; the one-year yielded 26.03% on November 5.
calls.view: The pound's move was the dollar's, not a loss of local support: foreigners bought about $570m of debt on Monday and remittances are at a record. A half-point Fed move would narrow the carry, so today's bill yields matter: a clear drop below 25% would signal the market pricing cuts that the Fed makes harder. The desk keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 (central bank sell rate) before December 9.

calls.headline: Nvidia drops 8.6% after hours as its board weighs removing Huang
calls.body: Nvidia rose 2.9% to $173.73 on Wednesday, then fell 8.6% in extended trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that its board would decide whether to remove Jensen Huang, its chief executive for 33 years; the New York Times reported a second affair, with an executive who reports to him (TechCrunch). The board met on Thursday and is working with an outside firm on candidates (Bloomberg). Taiwan's main index fell 2.6% on Thursday (Economic Daily News). Broadcom and AMD rose after hours. Nvidia reports results on November 17.
calls.view: A change at the top is now more likely than not to be decided before results, and either outcome leaves a gap: Huang runs about 60 direct reports with no named successor. That caps the stock until the board speaks and results show demand intact. The desk's chip view, judged Friday, will be right with Nvidia far below $220; the desk does not add a new bearish call, because the stock is 20% below its 50-day average and a clean report could lift it sharply.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $200 before its results on November 17.

calls.headline: CoreWeave's results revive the AI trade; Oracle jumps 8.8%
calls.line: Strong demand and cheaper financing eased the fear that AI data centers cannot pay their debts.
calls.body: CoreWeave rose 24.7% after third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.66bn and it raised its 2026 revenue outlook to up to $13.3bn, saying it will lean on loans backed by customer contracts rather than unsecured bonds (Yahoo Finance). The S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619.38 and the Nasdaq 1.60%. Oracle rose 8.8% to $128.38, Intel 7.5% to $62.50, Micron 11.9% and Broadcom 4.0% (Investing.com, MEXC). Stephens upgraded Oracle to overweight with a $213 target (Investing.com).
calls.view: The rally was relief about funding, which matters most for Oracle, whose debt-funded build-out had cost it a third of its value this year. One report does not end the debate, and Nvidia's turmoil after the bell shows how fragile the trade is; Oracle at $128.38 remains below its 50-day average of about $137.6.
calls.wrong: Oracle closes below $110 before the end of November.

Meta fell 2.0% to $628.77 as its infrastructure chief, Santosh Janardhan, said he would step down (TechCrunch via Yahoo Finance), and Amazon 1.7% to $266.17.
calls.view: A second day of losses on the launch says investors take the threat to Office seriously, and Microsoft is also a buyer of Anthropic shares at the IPO price. The desk sees Microsoft lagging the Nasdaq into Anthropic's listing, expected around November 19.
calls.wrong: Microsoft closes above $560, its record area, before November 20.

calls.headline: Dollar index reaches 102.84 as Fed hawks eye a half point
calls.line: Higher yields and a stronger dollar are the backdrop for every rally until December 9.
calls.body: The dollar index rose 0.6% to 102.84 on Wednesday, its highest since April 2025. Governor Waller said a 50-basis-point hike should be considered in December if October's prices matched the past two months (Federal Reserve); core prices rose 0.3%. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.98% on Tuesday before the Veterans Day bond holiday (Treasury). Gold fell 1.1% to $3,987, near its 52-week low. Producer prices come Friday.
calls.view: A quarter point is priced; the debate is now about a half point and more in 2027, which favors cash-rich steady earners over long-dated growth. Apple's record close shows the market still pays for cash flow. The desk expects the S&P 500 to hold above 7,250 into the meeting.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes below 7,250 before December 9.

view.headline: Bills and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: Wednesday's dip followed the dollar abroad, not a turn in local flows: foreign bill buying and record remittances still outweigh a firmer dollar, so the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–54 into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risks are a half-point Fed hike that cools the carry trade, core prices at home and export dollars lost to gas cuts.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or today's bills clear well below 24.5%, a sign of early rate cuts.
